questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $a^2+b^2+c^2=1$, then $a b+b c+c a$ lies in the interval
questions.solution:
We know, $(a+b+c)^2 \geq 0\begin{array}{lr}\Rightarrow a^2+b^2+c^2+2 a b+2 b c+2 c a \geq 0 \\ \Rightarrow 1+2(a b+b c+c a) \geq 0\end{array}
\Rightarrow \quad(a b+b c+c a) \geq \frac{-1}{2}...(i)
Also, \quad a²+b²+c²=1\begin{aligned} \text{$ and $} \Rightarrow a²+b²+c²-(a b+b c+c a) \\ \text{ and } \quad=\frac{1}{2}\left[(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2\right] \geq 0 \\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \quad 1-(a b+b c+c a) \geq 0\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad a b+b c+c a \leq 1$...(ii)
Hence, from Eqs. (i) and (ii),
$-\frac{1}{2} \leq$ a b+b c+c a \leq 1

questions.q: If $3^x+2^{2 x} \geq 5^x$, then the solution set for $x$ is
questions.solution:
We have, $\quad 3^x+2^{2 x} \geq 5^x\begin{aligned}
& 3^x+\left(2^2\right)^x \geq 5^x ; 3^x+4^x \geq 5^x \\
& \Rightarrow \quad\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^x+\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^x \geq 1
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad(\sin \theta)^x+(\cos \theta)^x \geq 1$
[by triangle inequality]
$\Rightarrow \quad x \leq 2\therefore$ Solution set is $(-\infty, 2]$

When $x>0$, then $\begin{aligned} & & |3 x+4| & =3 x+4 \\ \therefore & & 3^{3 x+4} & =3^{2(2 x-2)} \\ \Rightarrow & & 3 \hat{x}+4 & =4 \dot{x}-4 \\ \Rightarrow & & x & =8 \end{aligned}$

questions.q:
$\frac{1}{\log _{25} 10}+\frac{1}{\log _4 10}+\frac{1}{\log _{\sqrt{2}} 10}+\frac{1}{\log _{\sqrt{5}} 10} \text{$ is }$
equal to$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\log _{25} 10}+\frac{1}{\log _4 10}+\frac{1}{\log _{\sqrt{2}} 10}+\frac{1}{\log _{\sqrt{5}} 10} \\ = & \frac{\log 25}{\log 10}+\frac{\log \frac{4}{\log 10}}{\log }+\frac{\log \sqrt{2}}{\log 10}+\frac{\log \sqrt{5}}{\log 10} \\ = & \frac{2 \log 5+\frac{1}{2} \log 5}{\log 10}+\frac{2 \log 2+\frac{1}{2} \log 2}{\log 10} \\ = & \frac{5}{2}\left(\frac{\log 5+\log 2}{\log 10}\right)=\frac{5}{2} \frac{\log 10}{\log 10}=\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\log _2\left(9-2^x\right)=10^{\log (3-x)}$, solve for $x$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \text{Given, } \log _2\left(9-2^x\right)=10^{\log _{10}(3-x)} \\
& \Rightarrow \log _2\left(9-2^x\right)=(3-x) \ldots\left[\because a^{\log _a b}=1\right] \\
& \Rightarrow 2^{3-x}=9-2^x \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{2^3}{2^x}=9-2^x \\
& \Rightarrow 8=2^x \times\left(9-2^x\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 2^{2 x}-2^x \times9+8=0
\end{aligned} \)
Let \(2^x=y\), then
 \begin{aligned}& y²-9 y+8=0 \\
& \Rightarrow(y-8)(y-1)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow y=8 \text{ or } y=1 \\
& \Rightarrow 2^x=2^3 \text{ or }2^x=2^{{}^{\circ}} \\
& \Rightarrow x=3 \text{ or } x=0
\end{aligned}$$\)
But \(\mathrm{x}=3\) does not satisfy the given equation, since \(\log 0\) is not defined.$

Given that, $y=\frac{\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{2}}$ and $\quad x=\frac{\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{2}}$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & y=$\frac{1}{x}$ \\ \Rightarrow & x y=1\end{array}$
\begin{aligned}$& \therefore \quad 3 x²+4 x y-3 y²=3(x-y) (x+y)+4 x y\$end{aligned}\begin{aligned}$&=3$\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{2}}-\frac{\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{2}}\right)  \times\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{2}}+\frac{\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{2}}\right)+$4\$end{aligned}\begin{aligned}$& =3$\left[\frac{(\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{2})^2-(\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{2})^2}{(5-2)(5-2)}\right] \left[(\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{2})^$2+($\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{2})^$2\right]+4 \\ & =$\frac{1}{3} \cdot$4 $\sqrt{10} \cdot$2(5+2)+4 \\ & =$\frac{56}{3} \sqrt{10}+$4 \\ & =$\frac{1}{3}($56 $\sqrt{10}+$12)\end{aligned}
